parts.problem_md:
![Geometric diagram shows parallel lines AB and DE with intersecting triangle BCF. Angles marked are 39° at B and 63° at F. Angle x is within triangle.](assets/003-geometric-diagram-shows-parallel-lines-ab-and-de.png)

$ABC$ is parallel to $DEFG$
$BC=BF$ 
Angle $ABE=39^{\circ}$
Angle $CFG=63^{\circ}$

Work out the size of angle $x$. 
Give a reason for each stage in your working.
parts.solution_md:
> **[exam-tip]**
> When asked to find a missing angle you will commonly need to work out other missing angles first.
> 
> Write any calculated missing angles on the diagram provided making sure you write your method and reasons as you go.
> 
> Diagrams with parallel lines will often require you to use alternate, corresponding  and co-interior angle facts.

> *As lines **ABC** and **DEFG** are parallel, angles **BCF** and **CFG** are alternate angles and are therefore equal*

$BCF=CFG=63^{\circ}$

*because alternate angles are equal*

**[M1]**

> *Calculate angle **BFC** using the fact that base angles in an isosceles triangle are equal*

$BFC=BCF=63^{^{\circ}}$

*because base angles in an isosceles triangle are equal*

> *Calculate angle **CBF** using the fact that angles in a triangle add up to 180*<sup>*o*</sup>

`table row cell 180 minus open parentheses 63 plus 63 close parentheses end cell equals cell 180 minus 126 end cell row blank equals cell 54 to the power of degree space end exponent end cell end table`

*because interior angles of a triangle add up to 180°*

**[M1]**

> *Calculate angle *$x$* using the fact that adjacent angles on a straight line add up to 180*<sup>*o*</sup>

`table row cell 180 minus open parentheses 39 plus 54 close parentheses end cell equals cell 180 minus 93 end cell row blank equals cell 87 degree end cell end table`

*because adjacent angles on a straight line add up to 180°*

**[M1 A1 A1]**

**Final answer:** **87**<sup>**o **</sup>

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: Awarded for calculating either angle *BEF*=39<sup>o</sup> or angle *BCF*=63<sup>o</sup>
> 
> **M1**: Awarded for showing correct method for calculating either angle *CBF*=54<sup>o </sup>or angle *BFE*=54<sup>o</sup>
> 
> **M1**: Awarded for correct method to calculate angle $x$ and is still awarded if using previously incorrect values in correct method [e.g. 180-('39'+'54')].
> 
> **A1**: For $x$ correctly evaluated as 87<sup>o </sup>and at least one correct reason used and stated.
> 
> **A1**: For $x$ correctly evaluated as 87<sup>o</sup> and full correct reasons stated for your method used.

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows two congruent regular pentagons drawn inside a regular octagon.

![Octagon with two inner pentagons sharing vertex C. Angles A, B marked. Text on right: "Diagram NOT accurately drawn".](assets/002-octagon-with-two-inner-pentagons-sharing-vertex-.png)

One side of each pentagon lies along a side of the octagon.

$AB$ is a side of the octagon. 
$AC$ is a side of one of the pentagons. 
$BC$ is a side of the other pentagon.

Work out the size of angle $y$. 
Show your working clearly
parts.solution_md:
> *Calculate the sum of interior angles for a pentagon using *`open parentheses n minus 2 close parentheses cross times 180`

`open parentheses 5 minus 2 close parentheses cross times 180 equals 540`

> *Calculate one interior angle of a regular pentagon by dividing by the 5 equal angles*

$540\div5=108$

**[M1]**

> *Calculate the sum of interior angles for an octagon*

`open parentheses 8 minus 2 close parentheses cross times 180 equals 1080`

> *Calculate one interior angle of a regular octagon by dividing by the 8 equal angles*

$1080\div8=135$

**[M1]**

> *Triangle ABC is isosceles as it shares two of its side lengths with the regular pentagons, therefore angles CAB and ABC are equal*

> *Calculate angles CAB and ABC*

*135-108=27*

**[M1]**

> *Calculate angle *$y$*using the sum of angles in a triangle rule*

`180 minus open parentheses 27 plus 27 close parentheses equals 126`

**[M1]**

**Final answer:** $y=$**126**<sup>**o**</sup>

**[A1]**

parts.problem_md:
Here is a 9-sided regular polygon $ABCDEFGHJ$, with centre $O$

![Irregular polygon JABCDEFG with an interior triangle DEK and angle x° shown. Text indicates the diagram is not accurately drawn.](assets/004-irregular-polygon-jabcdefg-with-an-interior-tria.png)

$ODK$ and $FEK$are straight lines.

Work out the value of $x$
parts.solution_md:
> *Calculate angle **FOE**; it is an angle at the centre of a 9-sided regular polygon, so*

$\mathrm{angle}FOE=360\div9=40$

**[M1]**

> *You can use this to calculate angle **OFE**, as triangle **FOE** is an isosceles triangle*

$\mathrm{angle}OFE=\frac{180-40}{2}=70$

> *Angle** FOD** must be double angle **FOE*

$\mathrm{angle}FOD=40\times2=80$

**[M1]**

![An octagon labelled A to J with triangles OEF and DEK; angles are 40°, 70°, and x°. Note: Diagram not accurately drawn.](assets/005-an-octagon-labelled-a-to-j-with-triangles-oef-an.jpg)

> *Then calculate *$x$* using the sum of angles in triangle **FOK*

$180-70-80=30$

**Final answer:** **30**

**[A1]**

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows two triangles $ABE$ and $ECD$

![Triangle diagram with angles labeled: angle A is x degrees, angle D is 42 degrees, and angle at point B is 296 degrees. Note: Diagram not accurately drawn.](assets/007-triangle-diagram-with-angles-labeled-angle-a-is-.png)

Triangle $ABE$ is isosceles with $AE=EB$
$ADE$ and $EBC$ are straight lines.

Angle $CDE=42^{\circ}$
The reflex angle $ECD=296^{\circ}$
 Angle $BAE=x^{\circ}$

Work out the value of $x$

parts.problem_md:
The diagram below shows a triangle $PRQ$ and straight line $PQS$. The diagram is not drawn to scale.

- Angle `P R Q equals open parentheses 8 x plus 2 close parentheses degree`
- Angle `Q P R equals open parentheses 11 x plus 10 close parentheses degree`
- Angle `R Q S equals open parentheses 15 x plus 32 close parentheses degree`

![Triangle PQR with angles P (11x+10)° and R (8x+2)° and angle Q is missing. Angle (15x+32)°is adjacent to angle Q.](assets/001-triangle-pqr-with-angles-p-11x-10-and-r-8x-2-and.png)

Find the value of $x$
parts.solution_md:
An exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the other two interior angles of the triangle

`open parentheses 8 x plus 2 close parentheses plus open parentheses 11 x plus 10 close parentheses equals 15 x plus 32`

**[M1]**

Simplify the equation

*  *`table row cell 19 x plus 12 space end cell equals cell space 15 x space plus space 32 end cell row cell 4 x space end cell equals 20 end table`

**[M1]**

Solve

**Final answer:** **  **$x=5$

**[M1]**
